rows: The most accessible entry point. Pay depends heavily on whether you join an implementation partner (lower start, faster hands-on variety) or an in-house team at a large enterprise (steadier, sometimes higher base).
Meaningfully higher than Admin-only roles because Apex and LWC skill is scarcer. Requires genuine coding ability, not just completed Trailhead badges.
Pay climbs fastest here once you can run a discovery workshop and own a client relationship, not just configure what someone else designed.
The range widens a lot by employer type: boutique consulting partners and product companies pay meaningfully more than typical IT-services delivery teams at this stage.

items.heading: Most of the Job
items.text: Most of the job is configuration, process mapping, and stakeholder back-and-forth, not writing code, even Developer roles spend real time reading someone else's messy org before touching Apex.

items.heading: You Inherit Other People's Decisions
items.text: You inherit other people's decisions constantly. A production Salesforce org is rarely built cleanly from scratch; it is patched, re-patched, and half-documented by whoever came before you.

items.heading: The Ecosystem Moves in Three
items.text: The ecosystem moves in three release cycles a year. Staying current is a standing job requirement, not a one-time certification event.

items.heading: Client and Stakeholder Patience
items.text: Client and stakeholder patience is thin. Sales and service teams treat the CRM as their livelihood, so a broken flow or a bad deployment gets escalated fast.
